abstract: Currently, diabetes-induced skeletal muscle complications affect over half of diabetic patients yet the pathway by which this hyperglycemic damage occurs has yet to be fully elucidated. As such, the goal of this study is to investigate the hypothesis: Glucose-derived glycolaldehydes, glyoxal and methylglyoxal, formed in hyperglycemia cause damage to the skeletal muscle myoblasts through oxidative stress and formation of pro-inflammatory eicosanoids upon activation of phospholipase A2 (PLA2) and cyclooxygenase (COX). To test this hypothesis skeletal muscle myoblasts, C2C12s, were exposed to various concentrations of glyoxal and methylglyoxal then tested for metabolic activity, reactive oxygen species production, redox status, ATP production, membrane integrity, cellular proliferation, enzyme activity, and loss of mitochondrial lipids. Doses of the agonist at 1 mM and 2 mM showed significant changes in all tested areas and were significantly attenuated by NAC, Ibuprofen, AACOCF3 and metformin. For the first time, these results suggest a plausible pathway by which diabetes-induced skeletal muscle deterioration occurs and identifies possible therapeutic endpoints.
